entities.name: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib was the father of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. He was the son of Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim and Fatima bint Amr of the Makhzum Clan.

 Born in Mecca, Arabia, around 570 CE, Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib played a pivotal role in the early Islamic history. He was a prominent leader of the Quraysh tribe and a key figure in the Meccan trade and commerce. His leadership and influence extended beyond his tribe, shaping the politics and economy of the region. Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib's legacy continued to be felt long after his death, as his son Muhammad went on to unite the tribes and establish the Islamic Caliphate.

 His impact can also be seen in the spread of Islam, which began to take shape during his lifetime. The Prophet Muhammad's early teachings and revelations were primarily directed towards the Quraysh tribe, and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib's support and protection were crucial in this regard. The Prophet's message of monotheism and social justice resonated with the people, and soon, it spread to other parts of the Arabian Peninsula.

 Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib's life and legacy are also closely tied to the history of Mecca. He was a key figure in the city's development, and his leadership played a significant role in shaping its economy, politics, and culture. The city's importance as a center of trade and commerce was largely due to the leadership and vision of Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and his son Muhammad.
